newsitem.title: USA: Coca-Cola profits up 21 pct; PepsiCo net hurt by charge.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola profits up 21 pct; PepsiCo net hurt by charge.

text.p: Coca-Cola Co. said Tuesday its earnings jumped 21 percent in the latest quarter, thanks to strong soft drink sales, but rival PepsiCo Inc. reported a sharp drop in income due to a previously announced charge to restructure its international soft drink operation.
Coca-Cola said it earned $967 million, or 39 cents a share, in the third quarter versus year-ago earnings of $802 million, or 32 cents a share. Revenues slipped to $4.7 billion from $4.9 billion.
The Atlanta-based soft drink giant said unit case volume grew by 4 percent in North America, with the U.S. market posting a 5 percent rise.
It said Sprite was the fastest-growing U.S. soft drink brand while sales of POWERaDE, and Nestea were also up.

"Our U.S. business keeps on producing strong, profitable volume growth and share increases continuing the momentum we achieved in the first half of the year," said Roberto Goizueta, chairman and chief executive.
"The vast scope of our Olympic marketing activities over the past year generated significant rewards, and our strategy of package differentiation continues to be very successful," he said.
In Latin America, unit case volume rose 10 percent in the third quarter, compared with a 5 percent increase in the third quarter of 1995.
Unit case volume in the Middle and Far East was up 9 percent, on top of a 9 percent increase a year ago, it said.
In Africa, third-quarter unit case volume was flat following a 17 percent rise in last year's period, and European volume was up 1 percent after a 6 percent gain a year ago, Coca-Cola said.
PepsiCo said its earnings sank to $144 million, or 9 cents a share, in the quarter, compared with $617 million, or 39 cents a share, a year ago. Revenues rose to $7.9 billion from $7.7 billion.

The company, which announced in September that it would take charges totalling $525 million in the next two quarters to restructure its international beverage business, said it took a charge of $361 million from that planned restructuring in the third quarter.

The Purchase, N.Y.-based company said its worldwide beverage sales were off 1 percent to $2.8 billion, while worldwide snack food sales and profits rose 12 percent to $2.3 billion and $398 million, respectively.

It said worldwide restaurant sales were flat with the third quarter of 1995, but profits fell 9 percent due to poor domestic results at Pizza Hut. PepsiCo also operates the Taco Bell and KFC chain of fast food restaurants.
Coca-Cola's stock was off 75 cents at $48.375, while PepsiCo was unchanged at $29, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
